---
title: How SlideTAP removes items
subtitle: Which actions take items out of a project for good, and what to check before each one
---

When you leave something out of a submission in SlideTAP, it is not removed at
once. A de-selected item is removed from the project at the next
**Pre-process** or **Post-process**, and de-selecting one item can de-select
others with it. This page lists the actions that remove or lock data, what each
one does, and what to check before you click.

::: {.callout-note}
## Two versions of the pipeline

This page covers two versions of bp-submission-pipeline:

- **v3**: the `release/metadata-v3` line (SlideTAP 0.4). Its batch steps are
  **Search**, **Curate**, **Review**, **Unmapped**, **Pre-process**,
  **Post-process**, **Verify** (optional) and **Lock**. After those come
  **Store images** and **Export metadata** on the project's **Export** page.
- **v2**: the pipeline's `main` branch (SlideTAP 0.3). This is the version
  [H. Run a submission test](run-submission.qmd) walks through: Curate
  (step 4), Pre-process (step 5), Post-process (step 6), Validate (step 7),
  Complete (step 8) and Export (step 9).

Text without a label holds for both versions. Where they differ, the text says
so, v3 first, then v2.
:::

## What "removed" means

When SlideTAP removes an item, it deletes **its records in SlideTAP's
database**: the item itself (a sample, image, observation or annotation), its
metadata, and the comments and tags you added while curating it.

- Your **source slide files** are never touched.
- The **outbox** is never touched.
- SlideTAP's **own working copies** of the images (the files it downloads and
  converts) stay on disk until something larger is deleted. **v3:** they go
  when the whole batch is deleted. **v2:** deleting a batch leaves them; they go
  only when the whole project is deleted.

A removed item cannot be restored. To get it back you have to import it again
from the workbook, and importing into a project that already holds the rest of
the data has rules of its own. Treat every removal as final.

## Steps that change or remove data

One check applies before **and** after every step in the table: **count the
items per type**. In **Curate**, each type has its own tab, and the footer of
each table shows how many items it holds. Write the totals down, and compare
them with what you expect from the workbook. Nothing in the UI tells you when
items have gone; a count is the only way to see it. Step numbers in the table
are those of [H. Run a submission test](run-submission.qmd).

| Step | What it removes or locks | Check before you click |
|---|---|---|
| **Search**: parsing a workbook into a batch that already holds items (step 3) | Removes **every** item of that batch, curation included, before it imports the workbook again. Items that another batch still depends on are handed over to that batch instead. | That this is the batch you mean. If in doubt, create a new batch. Count items per type before and after. |
| **Pre-process** (step 5) | Removes every **de-selected** item of the batch from the project, then converts the images. | In Curate, open the deleted-items view (the recycle icon) on every type tab: everything listed there is about to go. Reload the page first, and count items per type before and after. |
| **Post-process**: the **Start** button (step 6) | Removes every item de-selected since pre-processing, the same way. | The same as for Pre-process. |
| **Lock** (v3) / **Complete** (v2, step 8) | Locks every item of the batch: from now on nothing in it can be edited, de-selected or restored. Every item has to be valid. **Reopen** on the project's **Batches** page undoes the lock, until the images have been stored. | That every failed image has been retried or de-selected, and the counts per type are what you expect. |
| **Store images** (v3 only, step 1 on the Export page) | Copies the selected images of every locked batch to the outbox. Removes nothing, but afterwards each batch is **Completed**: it can no longer be reopened or deleted. | That every batch is locked and counted. This is the last point at which a batch can still be reopened. |
| **Export metadata**: the **Submit** button (v3: step 2 on the Export page; v2: step 9) | Writes the metadata of **selected** items only. Nothing de-selected is exported, whether or not it has been removed. Removes nothing. | That the counts per type match what should be in the bundle. Afterwards, check the bundle as in step 9. |
| **Upload** ([J. Upload to BigPicture](upload.qmd)) | Changes nothing in SlideTAP, but what has been uploaded cannot be taken back from here. | That the bundle passed [I. Validate the bundle](validate.qmd), and its counts per type match the workbook. |
| **Delete** a batch (project's **Batches** page) | Removes the batch's items (see [Deleting a batch](#deleting-a-batch)). | That nothing in it is still wanted, and the counts per type of the other batches before and after. |

## De-selecting is a deferred delete

You de-select an item with:

- **Delete** on its row in **Curate**, or **Delete from project** on its item
  page. Despite the name, this only de-selects it.
- **v3:** **Delete** next to a failed image on the **Post-process** page.
- **v2:** **Exclude** in the image viewer of step 7, **Validate**.

A de-selected item is not deleted yet. It is listed in Curate's deleted-items
view (the recycle icon, "Toggle display of deleted items"), and **Restore**
puts it back.

That lasts only until the next **Pre-process** or **Post-process** of the
batch. Both begin by removing every de-selected item of the batch from the
project. A de-selected item is not "held back" for later: it is gone at the next
click on either button. The UI gives no warning, and the item disappears from
the deleted-items view as well.

The removal happens even when SlideTAP then refuses the click, for example on a
page left open from before, after the batch has already moved on. Reload the
page before you click either button.

::: {.callout-warning}
## In one production submission (v2)

The image items went from 25,015 at import to 21,962. **Pre-process** removed
2,811 images that a cascade (see the next section) had de-selected, together
with 418 samples and 442 observations. **Post-process** then removed 242 images
that had been de-selected by hand while they waited for a fix. Nothing in the UI
flagged either removal. It showed only when the items were counted per type
against the workbook.
:::

### De-selecting after post-processing

De-selecting an item after **Post-process** has finished removes nothing by
itself. The item is not stored to the outbox, and the export leaves it out,
because both take only selected items. It is removed only if Pre-process or
Post-process runs on the batch again.

**v3:** this is how you leave out an image that keeps failing. On the
**Post-process** page, click **Delete** next to the failed image, and the batch
can then be locked without it. That **Delete** is applied at once, **without**
the preview described below, and it still cascades. In the Bigpicture model, a
slide needs at least one image, so de-selecting a slide's only image also
de-selects that slide. If it was its block's only slide, the block goes too, and
so on upward. To see what goes with it first, de-select the image from its row
in **Curate** instead, where the preview shows it. Either way, count the items
per type afterwards.

**v2:** the equivalent is **Exclude** in step 7, **Validate**. It de-selects
only the image and the observations and annotations on it.

## De-selecting cascades

De-selecting one item can de-select related items, and that matters because of
the previous section. At the next Pre-process or Post-process, everything a
cascade de-selected is removed along with the item you chose.

**v3:** the cascade is deliberate, and it follows the rules of the data model:

- Each related item that the model no longer allows without the item is
  de-selected too, and so on outward through the hierarchy.
- An image, or a sample that sits under other samples, is de-selected once the
  last item it sits under goes.
- Before applying a selection that changes other items, SlideTAP shows a
  **preview** of what will change with it. This happens in **Curate** and on the
  item page. The dialog is titled "Remove ... from the project?". It lists the
  affected **Parents** and **Children** and says how many other items change
  with it.

*Worked example.* A block holds two slides, each with one image. You de-select
slide 2 in Curate. The preview lists the image of slide 2, which sits under that
slide only, and any observation on slide 2. The block stays, because it still
has slide 1. Later you de-select slide 1 too. Now the block has no slide left,
and the model says a block needs a slide, so the preview also lists the block.
If it was its specimen's only block, the specimen is listed as well, and so on
as far up as the model requires.

**Read the preview before you click Remove.** Once a Pre-process or
Post-process has run, everything listed in it is gone. If the preview reaches
further than you meant, click **Cancel**.

**v2:** there is no preview, and the cascade also reaches upward to items that
stay selected. De-selecting a sample de-selects the images and observations of
every sample above it (its block, specimen, case), even though those samples
themselves stay in the project. A diagnosis recorded on the specimen, for
example, is de-selected along with one slide. In one production submission,
counting beforehand showed that an exclusion of 679 items would also have
de-selected 54 observations, in a batch that had already been post-processed.
If you have to leave out many items in v2, count the items per type straight
after de-selecting, before anything else runs.

## Deleting a batch

You delete a batch on the project's **Batches** page, with **Delete** on its row.

**v3:**

- SlideTAP asks you to confirm in a **Delete batch?** dialog. The delete then
  runs in the background, and the batch shows as **Deleting** until it is gone.
- It is refused, and **Delete** is greyed out, for:
  - the **Default** batch;
  - a batch that is still running (searching, pre-processing,
    post-processing or storing images): wait for it to finish;
  - a **Curated and locked** batch: **Reopen** it first, on the same page;
  - a **Completed** batch: its images are in the outbox.
- It removes the batch's items and SlideTAP's working copies of its images.
  Source files and the outbox are left alone.

**v2:**

- There is no confirmation: the batch is deleted on the click. It is refused
  only for the **Default** batch.
- The delete runs inside the web request, and on a large batch that blocks the
  whole application until it finishes. In one production submission, deleting a
  batch of 22,889 images took about 75 minutes. The browser showed a 504 error,
  but the delete carried on in the background. Restarting the stack during it
  rolled the delete back. Wait for it to finish rather than restarting.
- The working copies of the batch's images stay on disk.

In both versions, samples and images that another batch's items still depend
on are **not** deleted. They move to the **Default** batch instead. They stay in
the project, and while they are selected they are part of the export.

## If every image fails pre-processing

**v3:** a batch counts as pre-processed once no image is still on its way,
whether the images succeeded or failed. Failed images can then be retried, or
de-selected.

**v2:** the batch was only checked for completion after an image succeeded. A
batch in which **every** image fails pre-processing therefore stays at **Image
Pre-processing** for good, and deleting the batch is the only way out.
